es: Interpretar gráficos de asistencia, pasos y temperaturas: reconocer verbos de tendencia, cifras aproximadas y proporciones.

teaching.en: As the chart shows, attendance rose steadily from 400 to 900 over the season.
teaching.es: Como muestra el gráfico, la asistencia subió de forma constante de 400 a 900 a lo largo de la temporada.
teaching.explanationEs: As the chart shows abre la descripción; rose steadily dice que subió sin saltos; from… to… da el inicio y el final.
segments: As the chart shows, attendance rose steadily
from 400 to 900 over the season.
teaching.audioText: As the chart shows, attendance rose steadily from 400 to 900 over the season.

teaching.en: Daily steps rose sharply by 20 percent in June, and that month was the peak of the year.
teaching.es: Los pasos diarios subieron bruscamente un 20 % en junio, y ese mes fue el punto máximo del año.
teaching.explanationEs: By + cifra dice cuánto cambió (en español «en un 20 %»). Peak es el punto más alto de la línea.
segments: Daily steps rose sharply by 20 percent in June,
and that month was the peak of the year.
teaching.audioText: Daily steps rose sharply by 20 percent in June, and that month was the peak of the year.

teaching.en: Temperatures fluctuate between 12 and 18 degrees in spring, so there is no clear trend.
teaching.es: Las temperaturas fluctúan entre 12 y 18 grados en primavera, así que no hay una tendencia clara.
teaching.explanationEs: Fluctuate describe una línea en zigzag; trend es la dirección general de la línea.
segments: Temperatures fluctuate between 12 and 18 degrees in
spring, so there is no clear trend.
teaching.audioText: Temperatures fluctuate between 12 and 18 degrees in spring, so there is no clear trend.

teaching.en: Roughly two thirds of the fans come by bus, so the majority travel together.
teaching.es: Aproximadamente dos tercios de los aficionados vienen en autobús, así que la mayoría viaja junta.
teaching.explanationEs: Roughly suaviza la cifra porque no es exacta. Majority significa más de la mitad, y dos tercios la superan.
segments: Roughly two thirds of the fans come
by bus, so the majority travel together.
teaching.audioText: Roughly two thirds of the fans come by bus, so the majority travel together.

teaching.en: Only a quarter of the students walk to school, and that proportion has not changed.
teaching.es: Solo una cuarta parte de los estudiantes va andando al colegio, y esa proporción no ha cambiado.
teaching.explanationEs: A quarter es el 25 %. Proportion es la parte que algo representa dentro del total.
segments: Only a quarter of the students walk to
school, and that proportion has not changed.
teaching.audioText: Only a quarter of the students walk to school, and that proportion has not changed.

es: Proyectar tendencias con prudencia: is set to, is projected to, is expected to reach y by then, más la duración con will have been + -ing.

teaching.en: The number of members is set to reach 1,200 by 2030.
teaching.es: Se prevé que el número de socios llegue a 1.200 en 2030.
teaching.explanationEs: Is set to + verbo base: los datos apuntan a que ocurrirá. By 2030 equivale a «para 2030».
segments: The number of members is set
to reach 1,200 by 2030.
teaching.audioText: The number of members is set to reach 1,200 by 2030.

teaching.en: Daily steps are projected to rise by 10 percent over the next decade.
teaching.es: Se proyecta que los pasos diarios suban un 10 % en la próxima década.
teaching.explanationEs: Is/are projected to + verbo base: proyección que sale de un cálculo; es lenguaje propio de informes.
segments: Daily steps are projected to rise by
10 percent over the next decade.
teaching.audioText: Daily steps are projected to rise by 10 percent over the next decade.

teaching.en: The club is expected to reach 50 teams, but the forecast could change.
teaching.es: Se espera que el club llegue a 50 equipos, pero la previsión podría cambiar.
teaching.explanationEs: Is expected to + verbo base dice lo que se espera. «Could change» añade prudencia.
segments: The club is expected to reach 50
teams, but the forecast could change.
teaching.audioText: The club is expected to reach 50 teams, but the forecast could change.

teaching.en: By 2030 the league will have been growing for ten years, so more growth is likely.
teaching.es: Para 2030 la liga llevará diez años creciendo, así que es probable que siga creciendo.
teaching.explanationEs: Will have been + -ing mide cuánto dura algo hasta un momento futuro. Likely = probable.
segments: By 2030 the league will have been growing
for ten years, so more growth is likely.
teaching.audioText: By 2030 the league will have been growing for ten years, so more growth is likely.

teaching.en: Current figures suggest the trend will continue, but this is only an estimate.
teaching.es: Las cifras actuales sugieren que la tendencia continuará, pero esto es solo una estimación.
teaching.explanationEs: Suggest + will es una proyección prudente; «only an estimate» avisa de que no es una certeza.
segments: Current figures suggest the trend will continue,
but this is only an estimate.
teaching.audioText: Current figures suggest the trend will continue, but this is only an estimate.

es: Comprobar si una afirmación está respaldada, exagerada o sin evidencia, y distinguir una correlación de una causa.

teaching.en: The claim that sleep improves grades is supported by evidence from two schools.
teaching.es: La afirmación de que dormir mejora las notas está respaldada por evidencia de dos colegios.
teaching.explanationEs: Supported by evidence: los datos dicen lo mismo que la afirmación, ni más ni menos.
segments: The claim that sleep improves grades is
supported by evidence from two schools.
teaching.audioText: The claim that sleep improves grades is supported by evidence from two schools.

teaching.en: Saying that every student improved is exaggerated: the data show gains for only seven out of ten.
teaching.es: Decir que todos los estudiantes mejoraron es exagerado: los datos muestran mejoras solo en siete de cada diez.
teaching.explanationEs: Exaggerated: hay datos, pero la frase dice más (every, always, all). The data va con verbo plural: show.
segments: Saying that every student improved is exaggerated: the data
show gains for only seven out of ten.
teaching.audioText: Saying that every student improved is exaggerated: the data show gains for only seven out of ten.

teaching.en: Sports injuries and temperature rise together in summer, but that is a correlation, not a cause.
teaching.es: Las lesiones deportivas y la temperatura suben juntas en verano, pero eso es una correlación, no una causa.
teaching.explanationEs: Dos cosas que suben a la vez tienen correlación; eso no prueba que una sea la causa de la otra.
segments: Sports injuries and temperature rise together in summer,
but that is a correlation, not a cause.
teaching.audioText: Sports injuries and temperature rise together in summer, but that is a correlation, not a cause.

teaching.en: Unlike last year, when attendance fell, this year it rose.
teaching.es: A diferencia del año pasado, cuando la asistencia cayó, este año subió.
teaching.explanationEs: Unlike + sustantivo o expresión de tiempo contrasta dos situaciones; no va seguido de una cláusula completa.
segments: Unlike last year, when attendance
fell, this year it rose.
teaching.audioText: Unlike last year, when attendance fell, this year it rose.

teaching.en: Girls' teams grew by 12 percent, whereas boys' teams grew by only 3 percent.
teaching.es: Los equipos femeninos crecieron un 12 %, mientras que los masculinos crecieron solo un 3 %.
teaching.explanationEs: Whereas une dos cláusulas completas que se contrastan; se puede usar while en su lugar.
segments: Girls' teams grew by 12 percent, whereas
boys' teams grew by only 3 percent.
teaching.audioText: Girls' teams grew by 12 percent, whereas boys' teams grew by only 3 percent.

teaching.en: The figures suggest that training time matters, but they do not prove it.

teaching.explanationEs: Suggest es un verbo prudente: apunta a una relación sin afirmar que esté demostrada.
segments: The figures suggest that training time matters,
but they do not prove it.
teaching.audioText: The figures suggest that training time matters, but they do not prove it.

es: Convertir una tabla de datos en una historia: tendencia con cifras, comparación, interpretación prudente y proyección, unidas con conectores.

teaching.en: Overall, the number of swimming sessions rose from two to three a week.
teaching.es: En general, el número de sesiones de natación subió de dos a tres por semana.
teaching.explanationEs: Overall abre el párrafo con la tendencia general; las cifras van después con from… to….
segments: Overall, the number of swimming sessions rose
from two to three a week.
teaching.audioText: Overall, the number of swimming sessions rose from two to three a week.

teaching.en: Compared with last year, the average heart rate of the runners fell by five beats.
teaching.es: En comparación con el año pasado, la frecuencia cardíaca media de los corredores bajó cinco pulsaciones.
teaching.explanationEs: Compared with + dato anterior introduce la comparación; average es la media, no una cifra concreta.
segments: Compared with last year, the average heart rate
of the runners fell by five beats.
teaching.audioText: Compared with last year, the average heart rate of the runners fell by five beats.

teaching.en: Meanwhile, the number of students who walk to school stayed almost the same.
teaching.es: Por su parte, el número de estudiantes que van andando al colegio se mantuvo casi igual.
teaching.explanationEs: Meanwhile contrasta dos líneas del gráfico que ocurren a la vez.
segments: Meanwhile, the number of students who walk
to school stayed almost the same.
teaching.audioText: Meanwhile, the number of students who walk to school stayed almost the same.

teaching.en: Runners tend to improve faster in spring, which appears to be linked to longer days.
teaching.es: Los corredores suelen mejorar más rápido en primavera, lo que parece estar relacionado con los días más largos.
teaching.explanationEs: Tend to y appear to son interpretaciones prudentes: dicen lo que sugieren los datos sin afirmar la causa.
segments: Runners tend to improve faster in spring, which
appears to be linked to longer days.
teaching.audioText: Runners tend to improve faster in spring, which appears to be linked to longer days.

teaching.en: If this trend continues, swimming is likely to overtake running by 2030; consequently, the pool may need longer hours.
teaching.es: Si esta tendencia continúa, es probable que la natación supere a correr en 2030; en consecuencia, la piscina quizá necesite más horas.
teaching.explanationEs: If this trend continues abre la proyección; overtake es superar a otro en una comparación; consequently añade la consecuencia, con may para la prudencia.
segments: If this trend continues, swimming is likely to overtake running
by 2030; consequently, the pool may need longer hours.
teaching.audioText: If this trend continues, swimming is likely to overtake running by 2030; consequently, the pool may need longer hours.

teaching.en: One interpretation is that the rise is partly due to the new pool.
teaching.es: Una interpretación es que el aumento se debe en parte a la piscina nueva.
teaching.explanationEs: Interpretation y partly señalan que es una lectura posible de los datos, no un hecho.
segments: One interpretation is that the rise is
partly due to the new pool.
teaching.audioText: One interpretation is that the rise is partly due to the new pool.

feedback.es: Overall resume la tendencia al empezar; meanwhile necesita una idea previa que contrastar y consequently necesita una causa.

prompt.es: Escribe un párrafo con tendencia, comparación y proyección prudente.

answer.text: Overall, the number of students who swim every week doubled between 2022 and 2025, rising steadily from 30 to 60. Compared with swimming, running hardly changed: around 55 students ran every week throughout those years. Meanwhile, the difference between the two activities has almost disappeared. The biggest rise came in 2025, when 13 more students joined. This appears to be partly linked to the new pool, although the data do not prove it. Swimming also tends to add around ten students a year. If this trend continues, swimming is likely to overtake running by 2026, and consequently the school may need longer pool hours. Of course, this is only an estimate, because next year's figures could be different.
accepted: Overall, the number of students who swim every week doubled between 2022 and 2025, rising steadily from 30 to 60. Compared with swimming, running hardly changed: around 55 students ran every week throughout those years. Meanwhile, the difference between the two activities has almost disappeared. The biggest rise came in 2025, when 13 more students joined. This appears to be partly linked to the new pool, although the data do not prove it. Swimming also tends to add around ten students a year. If this trend continues, swimming is likely to overtake running by 2026, and consequently the school may need longer pool hours. Of course, this is only an estimate, because next year's figures could be different.

Overall, the number of students who swim each week rose steadily from 30 in 2022 to 60 in 2025. In contrast, running stayed almost the same, at roughly 55 students, whereas swimming grew every year. The biggest jump came in 2025, when 13 more students started swimming. Running, by contrast, never changed by more than two students. It seems that the new pool may partly explain this rise, but the figures do not show the cause. Swimming tends to add roughly ten students each year. If the trend continues, swimming is expected to overtake running next year. Consequently, the school may have to offer more pool hours, although this is only a forecast.

prompt.es: Presenta el gráfico y responde con cautela a las dos preguntas del público.

answer.text: Good morning, everyone. I will briefly present the results of our school league. On this slide, the line illustrates the trend: the number of teams rose steadily from 12 in 2022 to 24 in 2025, so it doubled in three years. I'd like to highlight the jump between 2024 and 2025. Someone asked whether the league will keep growing. That is a fair question. If the trend continues, it is likely to reach thirty teams by 2027, but this is only an estimate. Another question was whether the new field caused the rise. The data suggest a link, but I can't say it is the cause, because the rise started earlier. One limitation is that we only have four years of data. Thank you for listening.

Hello, everyone. Today I will briefly present our school league. This slide shows that the number of teams grew steadily from 12 in 2022 to 24 in 2025. I would like to highlight the last year, when six new teams joined. You asked if the league will keep growing. That is a fair question: it is expected to reach thirty teams by 2027, but that is only an estimate. You also asked about the new field. The figures suggest a link, but I cannot say the field is the cause. One limitation is that we have only four years of data. Thank you, and I am happy to answer more questions.
